subject: Medexa: DPA routing, SCCs vs UK IDTA options and TIA scoping
messages:
From: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@medexa.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, procurement@medexa.com
Cc: Tom Bishop <tom.bishop@medexa.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Initial: DPA redline + cross-border routing questions

Hi Sean —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and procurement teams started a pass on Redwood's standard DPA and we attached a redline that highlights two areas we need to resolve before we can move to procurement:

1) International transfers: we operate in the UK and EU and need clarity on which mechanism Redwood expects us to sign for EU->US transfers. Your standard reference is SCCs, but our UK counsel wants to know if the UK IDTA + Addendum is acceptable or if you require a UK-specific signature.

2) Subprocessor visibility & risk: please confirm the list of subprocessors that will process Medexa customer data and indicate whether any third parties have access to raw clinical notes.

We attached the redline (Medexa_DPA_redline.docx) and our subprocessors matrix for your reference. Can you also share your SOC 2 snapshot to speed security onboarding?

Target timeline from our side is to close the DPA and routing approach by 11/20 so procurement can issue the PO by month-end. Would Redwood be available for a short call this week to resolve routing and fallback options (SCCs vs IDTA vs TIA)?

Thanks,
Ava Reynolds
Head of Legal Operations
Medexa Health
Attachment: Medexa_DPA_redline.docx (docx)
Attachment: medexa_subprocessors_list.csv (csv)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@medexa.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial: DPA redline + cross-border routing questions

Hi Ava —

Appreciate the clear redline and the timeline. Quick answers up front, then proposals for next steps:

- Mechanism: Redwood can accept either the EU SCCs or the UK IDTA + Addendum. For operational simplicity we typically request (1) SCCs for EU-to-US data flows, and (2) the UK IDTA + Addendum for processing obligations involving UK-law data subjects. If you prefer a single approach across both jurisdictions we can provision a dual-signature workflow (SCCs + UK Addendum) but that will add ~3 business days to legal review.

- Subprocessors: we do maintain a current subprocessors inventory — I'll attach the exported CSV and a SOC2 snapshot in a follow-up. No external subprocessor has routine access to raw clinical notes; access is limited to specific, audited subprocessors for storage and logging.

Proposed next steps:
1) Internal sync call (30 min) with Medexa legal + procurement, Redwood Legal (Marissa) and Privacy (Kimberly) — propose 11/10 at 9:00am PT.
2) If Medexa wants to avoid dual-signing, we can prepare a TIA (Transfer Impact Assessment) addendum scoped to your data flows and pseudonymization controls; this requires a brief questionnaire and a follow-up remediation plan if high-risk transfers are identified.
3) I'll upload an annotated response to each redline comment in Drive (link below) and add our preferred clause language where needed.

Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/Medexa-DPA-2026
DocuSign (sample template): https://app.docusign.com/envelope/12345678-abcdef

I'll attach the Redwood_subprocessors_export and a SOC2 snapshot in my next message. If 11/10 9:00am PT works we can lock the call and resolve the mechanism then.

Best,
Sean
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: (will follow)

Sean — thanks for the quick reply and for looping in Marissa and Kimberly. 11/10 9:00am PT works for Medexa; I'll send calendar invites.

Answers to a couple of your questions up front:
- We'd prefer a single-signature path if possible (avoid dual-signing). If Redwood's TIA approach can reasonably reduce evidentiary burden while preserving our UK counsel's comfort, that's our preference.
- I'll bring our internal TIA questionnaire and the data flow diagram to the call.

Attaching our SOC2 snapshot and a simplified data-flow diagram to help focus the scoping discussion. Expect the procurement PO to be contingent on DPA + routing alignment.

See you on the call — calendar invite (will send).

Ava

Attachment: medexa_dataflow_v2.png (png)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Medexa DPA — clause proposals & next steps (RE: call notes)

Marissa / Kim —

Summary from the call and suggested drafting approach:

1) Mechanism recommendation: propose we offer Medexa a TIA-scoped approach paired with the EU SCCs OR UK IDTA (single-signature option): we will prepare a short TIA questionnaire that limits the scope to the specific categories in their dataflow (ingest -> ephemeral inference -> encrypted logs). If no high-risk transfers surface, we will accept a single signature where the customer signs the SCCs and we append the TIA as an operational exhibit.

2) Clause language: replace Medexa's proposed "data localization carve-out" line with this fallback: "Where transfers are covered by a TIA that materially reduces residual risk through technical and contractual safeguards (including continuous pseudonymization and limited KV cache retention), Redwood and Customer agree that SCCs (as adopted by EU Commission) shall govern transfers and no additional UK-only signature is required." Please confirm legal comfort with that language or propose edits.

3) Subprocessor assurance: provide the exported list (attached earlier) and offer a 30-day notice window for subprocessor changes. Emphasize that no subprocessors have routine access to raw clinical notes; any access is strictly timeboxed and audited.

4) Next actions for legal ops: Marissa to prepare redline with above clause and a 1-page TIA questionnaire. Kimberly to draft a short evidence checklist we can request during onboarding (SOC2 snapshot already received). I'll coordinate with Ava to produce a DocuSign envelope if Medexa confirms single-signature preference.

I'll drop the DPA draft and a one-pager TIA into the shared Drive by EOD.

Thanks,
Sean
